source.title: Do Sparse Autoencoders Capture Concept Manifolds?
source.authors: Usha Bhalla; Thomas Fel; Can Rager; Sheridan Feucht; Tal Haklay; Daniel Wurgaft; S. Boppana; M. Kowal; Vasudev Shyam; Jack Merullo; Atticus Geiger; E. Lubana

record.tranche_reason: The paper tests sparse autoencoder representations of superposed manifolds and argues that current SAE atoms often tile manifold structure rather than capturing it as a compact, coherent group. This refines the one-direction account, though it does not reproduce the original Toy Models of Superposition experiment.
record.gate_note: The synthetic sparsity sweep and Llama SAE measurements bear on the versions recorded below. The paper also reports activation steering along raw Llama manifolds and compares feature-similarity metrics; these do not directly establish SAE feature behavior for the claim versions. Random-orthogonal/PCA and random-SAE comparisons appear in figures, but the text does not describe their results numerically.
record.test_reason: In Llama3.1-8B (layer 19), the paper shows concept manifolds that SAE atoms tile rather than capture compactly. It also shows individual SAE features are unstable across SAEs while manifold-level coordinates align. These results argue that V5 (SAE features as canonical units) and V6 (1-D superposed features) need restating. The synthetic benchmark trains SAEs on constructed manifold mixtures, not toy networks that learn superposition, so it does not test V1.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say SAEs preserve geometry only implicitly. On Llama SAEs, manifolds sit in a 'dilution' regime: they are tiled by many localized, partially redundant atoms rather than captured as a compact subspace. Individual features are unstable across SAEs, but manifold-level coordinate systems are consistent. Interpretability should treat groups of features and geometric objects as the units.
record.recipe_differences: The study develops a synthetic sparse-mixture-of-manifolds benchmark and measures SAE manifold capture, then analyzes SAE representations in Llama3.1-8B. It does not reproduce the original toy-model feature-superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The synthetic capture regime changes with SAE sparsity. In Llama measurements, receptive-field partitions vary by SAE architecture; the paper also compares expansion factors and sparsities.

fits_no_version.finding: In synthetic sparse mixtures of known manifolds, TopK SAEs recover each manifold's subspace compactly only near k≈4. At lower k they shatter it; at higher k they dilute it across redundant atoms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE recovery of multi-dimensional structure depends on the SAE sparsity budget matching the structure's embedding dimension.

fits_no_version.finding: Decoder cosine similarity and Pearson correlation fail to group a manifold's features; Ising couplings and conditional co-activation succeed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Membership of multi-dimensional features is revealed by co-activation, not decoder geometry.

record.problems: Most plotted findings in the supplied text have no reported numeric values or uncertainty estimates. The LLM analysis is limited to Llama3.1-8B layer 19 and averages several SAE results for key capture measurements. The study does not test the original near-orthogonal toy-feature claim directly.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports raw-activation steering along several manifolds (Section 3; Figure 2), but this is not an SAE feature measurement and does not directly test the recorded versions. It also compares five feature-similarity metrics for grouping manifolds (Section 6; Figure 9), a manifold-discovery result rather than a direct result on these versions.

untested.parts: All of it: no small network is trained to compress more sparse features than dimensions. The synthetic setup builds the mixture by hand and its total embedding dimension (126) fits within d=128.
All of it: no test of importance or capacity allocation.
Whether LLM features are spread across neurons, or whether the model contains sparse features an SAE recovers. SAEs are only selected for variance explained above 0.85.
Completeness of the dictionary, and models or layers other than Llama3.1-8B layer 19.
Whether the manifolds are irreducibly multi-dimensional, and concepts outside the templated continuous ones.

missing.what: PCA shows curved manifold geometry for days (circle), colors (paraboloid), years (helix), etc. Steering between centroids changes token probabilities smoothly, showing the geometry is causally used. This is direct evidence for V6 that no row records.
Comparison of trained SAEs against the PCA, random-orthogonal and random-SAE baselines in restricted-support curves and tuning curves.
Mixed-selectivity tuning curves for the colors (hue) and sentence-length manifolds.
Claim that Llama SAE Ising couplings within manifold groups have mixed sign (dilution); stated in the text, no figure or number given.

record.verdict_notes: None of the rows is from the original source, so verdicts are allowed. The reader's V1 support verdict is dropped because the synthetic benchmark is an SAE-recovery test on hand-built data, not a toy superposition network. The reader's V4 support verdict is dropped because SAE quality is only a selection criterion. All key results are figure-only and no uncertainty is reported. The LLM work covers one model and one layer.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the original toy-model setup or whether sparse features are nearly orthogonal, nor does it sweep feature importance. Its synthetic experiments instead study sparse mixtures of curved manifolds and SAE capture regimes.
The study does not test whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions or explains polysemanticity.
The study does not test polysemanticity arising from mechanisms other than capacity pressure.
The LLM evidence concerns SAEs on Llama3.1-8B at layer 19; it does not establish feature distributions across other models or show that features are sparse across neurons generally.
The study compares SAE features across models and training choices, but does not establish completeness or canonical status for every possible feature or representation.

The study does not compare a model whose primitive superposed features are intrinsically multidimensional against one whose primitives are one-dimensional; its evidence concerns curved manifolds represented by collections of one-dimensional SAE atoms.

rows.subject: TopK SAE (synthetic benchmark)
rows.size_stated: dictionary size c=512; ambient dimension d=128
rows.operation_detail: Measured restricted R2 for manifold reconstruction across SAE sparsity budgets.

conditions.value: average across eight manifold types and 48 instances

rows.measure: Restricted R2 for reconstruction using a restricted number of atoms
rows.value: Figure only; the text says capture peaks near k = 4 and degrades at both lower and higher sparsity.
rows.note: The result supports a sparsity-dependent capture regime in this synthetic manifold benchmark. It does not measure near-orthogonality of feature directions.
rows.check: Subject is a TopK SAE fit to constructed data, not a small network that learns superposition. The sparsity sweep is SAE k, not feature sparsity, so it does not bear on V1's transition. Also, the summed embedding dims (21 per variant × 6 = 126) do not exceed d=128, so by the paper's own definition the data are not superposed. Belongs in fits_no_version.

rows.subject: TopK SAE (synthetic benchmark)
rows.size_stated: dictionary size c=512; ambient dimension d=128
rows.operation_detail: Tracked support size and receptive-field spread across sparsity budgets to characterize capture regimes.

conditions.value: low, intermediate, and high k; exact plotted values are figure only

rows.value: Figure only; the text describes low-k shattering, intermediate-k compact capture, and high-k dilution with redundant active atoms.
rows.note: The reported regimes concern how SAEs represent curved manifolds, not the regular geometry or near-orthogonality claimed for the original toy models.
rows.check: Same as R1: the shattering/capture/dilution regimes describe SAE recovery of constructed manifolds, not V1's geometry of features learned in superposition. Figure only, no numbers.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction quality as the number of selected SAE features increased.
rows.measure: Restricted R2 / variance explained as a function of restricted support size
rows.value: Figure only; the text says variance explained plateaus at a support size well beyond each manifold's ambient dimension.
rows.note: The paper interprets this as manifold geometry being distributed across a larger, partially redundant feature set rather than a compact group.
rows.check: Not a V4 result: the 0.85 variance-explained filter is a selection criterion, and the row measures how SAE atoms organise manifolds, not whether sparse features exist. Fig. 6 plots PCA, random-orthogonal and random-SAE baselines, but the record says the baseline is not stated. Values are averaged across SAEs and figure only.

source_check.correct: Compact manifold capture is absent under the restricted-support protocol. For V6, the state is cannot_determine: reconstruction support size does not establish the dimensionality of the underlying superposed features.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5, compact-capture paragraph; Figure 6; Appendix B.2 model selection.
source_check.problem: The shared absent state overextends failure of compact SAE capture to absence of one-dimensional underlying features.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Plotted SAE feature activations along the years manifold.

conditions.value: BatchTopK, TopK, JumpReLU, Standard (ℓ1), Matryoshka, and Random

rows.measure: Feature activation tuning curves across year values
rows.value: The text reports localized, smooth activation patterns with overlapping support; most SAEs show features for the ones digit and others for the decade.
rows.note: The paper describes the manifold as covered by multiple selective features rather than a single feature encoding the full variable.
rows.check: Drop V4. The atoms are selective (ones digit, decade), but per the text only their joint activity encodes the year variable. A Random SAE is also plotted as a control, with no comparison in the text.

source_check.correct: Localized, overlapping tuning curves and joint encoding support the stated qualification of V5. For V6, this measurement is cannot_determine: SAE tuning curves alone do not establish the dimensionality of the underlying superposed features.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5, tiling-selectivity paragraphs; Figure 7 and caption.
source_check.problem: The V6 state conflates localized SAE responses with a test of underlying feature dimensionality.

rows.subject: Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Visualized the highest-activating SAE feature across sampled points in the ambient space of the days manifold.

conditions.value: BatchTopK, TopK, JumpReLU, Standard (ℓ1), Matryoshka, and Random

rows.measure: Feature receptive-field selectivity in ambient space
rows.value: Figure only; the text describes feature selectivity for each day and says architectural assumptions produce different partitions of the ambient space.
rows.note: The text describes different architectural biases, including angular separability for TopK and linear separability for ℓ1.
rows.check: Drop V4. Figure only. The partition of the days manifold depends on SAE architecture (angular for TopK, linear for ℓ1).

source_check.correct: Architecture-dependent partitions qualify V5. For V6, the receptive-field comparison is cannot_determine: it measures SAE partitioning rather than underlying feature dimensionality.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5, ambient-space sampling paragraphs; Figure 8 and caption.
source_check.problem: Architecture-dependent receptive fields do not themselves measure whether the underlying superposed features are one-dimensional.

rows.subject: SAEs trained on Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared features across SAEs using optimal transport in decoder-direction space.
rows.value: The text reports weak alignment, particularly for point-based methods such as SpaDE.
rows.note: The authors say individual feature identity depends strongly on architecture and training dynamics.
rows.check: The text says 'individual features are not stable objects' from weak decoder-space alignment. Figure only. The comparison includes SpaDE, which failed the variance-explained threshold.

rows.subject: SAEs trained on Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature activations across models using optimal transport on random training inputs.
rows.value: Figure only; the text says there is slightly more consistent structure than in decoder space, but no clear alignment.
rows.note: The comparison does not show stable one-to-one feature identities across SAEs.
rows.check: No clear alignment of codes on random data. Figure only.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix B.3; Figure 13, random-data code-space comparison.

rows.subject: SAEs trained on Llama3.1-8B
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE codes across models using optimal transport restricted to points on a given manifold.
rows.measure: Cross-SAE alignment of manifold-specific coordinate systems
rows.value: The text reports strong alignment across SAEs when comparisons are restricted to specific manifolds.
rows.note: The paper attributes the alignment to the geometric structures collectively encoded, not to stable individual features.
rows.check: Stability holds for manifold-level coordinate systems (formality, violence, geography in Fig. 13), not for individual features. Figure only.

source_check.locator_found: Appendix B.3, final paragraph; Figure 13, manifold-specific comparisons.

relationships.condition: Llama3.1-8B layer 19: individual SAE features compared across architectures and training runs
relationships.reason: Decoder and random-data code alignment is weak or unclear across SAEs (R6, R7). Manifold reconstruction needs a support well beyond the manifold's ambient dimension rather than a compact atom group (R3).
relationships.display_finding: Decoder and random-data code alignment was weak or unclear across SAEs, and reconstructing a manifold needed a support well beyond its ambient dimension rather than a compact group of atoms.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Llama3.1-8B layer 19: individual SAE features compared across architectures and training runs
source_check.reason: R6–R7 and Appendix B.3 explicitly report unstable individual features and weak or unclear alignment. Architectural comparisons substantiate the label; a separately controlled training-seed comparison is not documented.

relationships.condition: Llama3.1-8B layer 19: comparisons restricted to points on specific manifolds
relationships.reason: Manifold-level coordinate systems align strongly across SAEs, so stability holds for feature groups, not single atoms (R8). Atom partitions vary by architecture (R5), and atoms act as localized tiles (R4).
relationships.display_finding: Coordinate systems for whole manifolds aligned strongly across SAEs, but atoms acted as localized tiles whose partition varied by architecture, so stability held for feature groups rather than single atoms.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Llama3.1-8B layer 19: comparisons restricted to points on specific manifolds
source_check.reason: R8 reports consistent manifold-level coordinate systems despite individual-feature differences; R4–R5 show localized, architecture-dependent tilings. Stability therefore requires qualifying the proposed unit of representation.

relationships.condition: Llama3.1-8B layer 19, templated continuous concepts (years, days, colors, temperature, age)
relationships.reason: Concepts lie on curved multi-dimensional manifolds (Sec. 3, text). 1-D SAE atoms only tile them as localized detectors, and capture needs many atoms (R3, R4, R5). Irreducibility of the manifolds is not tested.
relationships.display_finding: The concepts lay on curved multi-dimensional manifolds that 1-D SAE atoms only tile as localized detectors, with many atoms needed to capture each one; irreducibility of the manifolds was not tested.

relation.reason: Its own experiments test SAE feature stability and organization, alongside concept geometry in Llama3.1-8B.

tranche.reason: The paper directly argues for revising individual-direction interpretations using fragmented manifold capture, architecture-dependent tiling, and unstable individual SAE features.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is faithful. V6 geometric evidence belongs in a separate Section 3/Figure 2/Table 1 row; model-wide prevalence and irreducibility remain untested, and the synthesis-wide count of 26 cannot be verified from this study.

statements.correction: Appendix B, Table 1: years—helix; days—circle; colors—paraboloid; temperature—line; age—line. Section 5: localized, overlapping year responses; manifold reconstruction distributed across atoms. Section 3: geometric structure and steering effects. Irreducibility untested.
statements.problem: The tiling and joint-activity findings are accurate, but the condition group includes geometries classified as lines. SAE fragmentation alone does not demonstrate multidimensional underlying features.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: synthetic sparse mixtures of curved manifolds
reader_labels.reason: The sparsity sweep shows a capture sweet spot and qualitatively different low-, intermediate-, and high-sparsity regimes (R1, R2); it does not test near-orthogonality.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The reported LLM measurements show manifold reconstruction requiring many features and localized, overlapping feature responses (R3, R4, R5).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: cross-SAE comparisons, especially decoder directions and random-data codes
reader_labels.reason: Individual features show weak or unclear alignment across SAEs, while manifold-specific coordinate systems align strongly (R6, R7, R8).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The paper reports curved manifold structure represented through collections of localized atoms, with reconstruction requiring support beyond the manifold's ambient dimension (R3, R4, R5).
